rendered: The premise is not what the paper concludes. It does not say aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[1]. It concludes the opposite, in its own words: "Overall, this work clearly demonstrates that aqueous processing is compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[2]." Lithium leaching is presented as minimal, not disqualifying: the percentage of leached Li+ rises with nickel content, but even Ni-rich NMC 811[3] shows only minimal leaching, about ~3 wt%[4] after a week. Aqueous-processed NMC 811[5] cells still show very good cycling, with capacity retention of ~70%[6] versus ~76%[7] for NMP-processed cells. Other NMC 811[8] aqueous-processing issues (Li/H+ exchange, a highly basic solvent pH, and surface morphology changes) arise only if formulation chemistry is not handled properly; the paper does not present them as making aqueous processing incompatible.
